main_text.p: thena, Maledicti. Farwatbanuall, Abominatione. Farwet, Abominatus] ropcuꝯ & ꝑnacoo, Saxon. Nequam, Pravus, Vilis, Turpis.
Farfeggent, Excusandos] Forte à far, Sax.ꝑop, Teut. Aer, pro, & seg-gben, Sax.ꝑecꝯean, dicere.
Fattira, Munita] Huic affine Sax, ꝑæꝓtene, ꝑæꝓtnyꝓꝓe, ꝑæꝓtnunꝯe, quæ omnia munitione, municipiu, &c. signant: unde nostrum fast, Teuton. bast, pro firmus; item to fasten, id est, firmare, & simil.
Felts, Rupem] Saxonibus olim & nobis hodieque stints, silices. Vide Kilian.in belt.
Ferreno, Longè: nos Aerre] Sax. ꝑeoꝓp; nos farre, Germ.ferr.
Ferthe, Excessu] Huic affine nostratium sorth, quod à Sax. ꝑapan, i.e. ire, venit, quibus ꝑopꝓzanꝯ, pro processus; item ꝑopꝓꝓape, pro obitus, vel exitus.
Fetberacco, Alarum: nos Aederen] Nos feathers, à Saxon. ꝓyꝯena, id est, alæ, pennæ.

page.notes: Handwritten marks in the right margin and a few faint stains are not transcribed. Several Old English words are uncertain and may be misread; the Saxon glosses in this page are partly illegible.
